title: Bob's bit recovered from the disjoint coordinate vector
statement: Let $\omega$ be a sample of the hard distribution lying in the disjoint event — that is, one whose induced input sets $X(\omega)$ and $Y(\omega)$ are disjoint. Then for every coordinate $i$, the Bob-bit of the disjoint coordinate assigned to $i$ by the generated coordinate-pair vector agrees with Bob's bit $\mathrm{yBit}(\omega, i)$ at that coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: sample ω lies in the disjoint event (X(ω) and Y(ω) are disjoint)
replaced: On disjoint samples, the generated coordinate vector recovers Bob's input bit at every coordinate.
